subject: Proposal: Renewal + Dedicated Capacity Expansion (A100→H100/L40S) — value & timeline
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Shaw <rebecca@echelon.ai>, Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@echelon.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation + proposal for dedicated expansion and hardware regrade

Rebecca / Alex —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Echelon’s agent usage has grown ~2.3x year-over-year and your renewal is coming up in December. Based on observed traffic patterns and the latency targets you shared (95th pctl latency < 250ms for LLM-chat workloads), we recommend the following as a starting point for the renewal:

- Term: 12 months renewed from 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31 with ability to early scale
- Reserved pool: increase from 32 A100 GPUs → 48 H100 GPUs (or 48 L40S as an alternative for batch-heavy pipelines)
- Throughput guarantee: baseline capacity to support 1.2B tokens/day (with automatic burst to 1.6B) and a 99.9% availability target for the Dedicated pool
- Performance-per-dollar: our internal bench (attached) shows H100 delivers ~1.7x tokens/sec vs A100 for your model mix and a net ~1.35x throughput-per-dollar with recommended quantization profiles

I’ve attached a concise proposal PDF and the raw benchmark CSV. If you prefer L40S for certain batch jobs we can split the pool and offer a blended rate.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick call to run the numbers with your finance/infra; 2) Redwood to provide a 2-week test window on H100 (canary) before final cutover; 3) sign updated order form and amended SOW.

Can you confirm who from your procurement/infra team should be on the call? Happy to schedule this week or early next.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Rebecca Shaw <rebecca@echelon.ai>

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + proposal for dedicated expansion and hardware regrade

Ben —

Thanks for the overview and the attachments. A few quick clarifying questions before we pull in procurement:

1) Can you break down the cost delta for H100 vs A100 at our committed utilization (we’re seeing ~65% sustained utilization across peak months)?
2) For the suggested throughput guarantee, what is the remediation if Redwood misses the target? Service credits?
3) We run two main workloads: (a) low-latency interactive agents (chat), (b) nightly batch re-ranking and embedding reprocessing. Would you recommend migrating chat to H100 and leaving batch on A100, or splitting into H100+L40S?

If you can send a short one-pager with the perf-per-dollar numbers and recommended pool split, we’ll be able to get procurement in the room.

—Rebecca
VP, Product — Echelon Robotics

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Shaw <rebecca@echelon.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + proposal for dedicated expansion and hardware regrade

Rebecca —

Appreciate the clear questions. Short answer up front: for your model mix we recommend a hybrid pool — move the low-latency interactive agents to H100 and route nightly batch to L40S or a cost-tiered A100 pool. Below is the perf-per-dollar summary and remediation language we propose; full tables are in the attached CSV.

Perf-per-dollar (summary at ~65% utilization, model family: seq-20k/chat-7b-ish):
- H100 (FP16 + q4_0 where applicable): ~1.7x tokens/sec vs A100 (FP16). After accounting for instance-hour pricing and expected price per token, H100 yields ~1.35x throughput-per-dollar for interactive workloads due to better kernel efficiency and reduced memory fragmentation.
- L40S (INT8/TF32 optimized): for large batch jobs L40S gives ~2.0x throughput vs A100 on INT8 paths; cost-per-token is ~1.5x better than A100 when using batch-optimized quantization and mixed-precision inference.
- Migration overhead: estimated 2–3% billable uplift during the 2-week canary (reserved burn-in/testing). We bake that into the proposal pricing.

Recommended pool split for renewal pricing example (proposed 48 GPUs total):
- 28 H100 GPUs for chat (dedicated low-latency pool, can autoscale within reserved headroom)
- 12 L40S GPUs for nightly batch and large embedding runs
- 8 A100 fallback nodes for legacy pipelines and compatibility (keeps risk low)

Throughput guarantee + remediation:
- Objective: baseline 1.2B tokens/day with 4-hour rolling buffer for burst up to 1.6B
- Remedy: if Redwood fails to meet the guaranteed capacity on a rolling 30-day window, we provide service credits up to 15% of the monthly reserved fee and will supply priority remediation (engineering warroom).

Attachments included: concise proposal PDF, raw perf CSV, and a migration MAP (action plan). I’ll also drop an internal note to the infra team about capacity scheduling.

Proposed next: 30-minute call with procurement (you + Alex + procurement), Redwood finance + soojin from infra. I have availability Thur 11/05 10:00–11:30 PT or Fri 11/06 14:00–16:00 PT. Which works?

Thanks,
Ben
[attachment: MAP-e2e-plan-Echelon-20261116.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Echelon renewal — pricing cadence & negotiation points

Team —

Thread: Echelon (RDW-ECHE-2026-11) — they asked for perf-per-dollar and remediation details. I sent the hybrid recommendation and three proposed pool split. Key asks from their side: explicit cost delta at 65% utilization, procurement in the call, and strong remediation language.

Negotiation playbook:
- Offer a 4% partner credit for the first 3 months of the renewal if they sign the 12-month + 48-GPU commit (sweetener to offset migration uplift).
- Keep remediation language but cap credits at 15% monthly as Ben proposed — maintain SLA language for enterprise customers.
- Provide a 2-week no-cost canary on H100 (we absorb the burst cost to show delta). This is important for procurement acceptance.
- For pricing, suggest blended rate: 0.92x per-GPU-hour for H100 relative to A100 list (after reserved discount) so blended pool vends ~1.2x effective performance vs their current baseline at ~1.15x cost.

Marissa: can you prepare the updated order form with those credits & blended rates? Dylan: please confirm inventory availability in us-west-2 for 48 GPUs across H100/L40S/A100 mix and lead time (target cutover by 2027-01-15).

Ben
